messages.subject: Cooler bag defect
messages.text:
Hello
 

 I was all set to write you a 5 star review after taking my brand new cooler bag to a cabin and having a head of lettuce emerge fresh as a daisy after spending two days in the bag with an ice pack to keep it cold. Fantastic!

 

 However, the second time I used the bag I put in 2 bags of frozen blueberries weighing a total of 3.2 kilos and 2 ice packs, closed the bag, picked it up and the plastic buckle keeping it closed snapped. See pictures. Because of all the stress put on this
 point, this buckle should be made of something much more substantial than a 3D printed piece of plastic. I am now trying to source metal ones to replace all the plastic that came with the bag. 

 

 I’m also not sure why the little pillowy piece that goes on the bottom of the bag wasn’t completely lined in vinyl. After the first use I noticed a big stain on the bottom of it. Not sure how to clean it, but it looks gross. Again, see pictures. 

 

 I was excited to support a new environmentally conscious company that both designs and manufactures in Canada so am very disappointed in some of the finishes on your product. I am reaching out to you to see if there is a fix for these issues rather than
 just leave a crappy review. It’s hard enough when a company is first starting out, so I do want to encourage you to do what you can to make a product that consumers will be happy purchasing. 

 

 Regards,

 Angela Stoner

 

 Sent from my iPhone

messages.subject: Re: Cooler bag defect
messages.text:
Hi Angela! 
 

 We are really sorry for that. 
 

 Some of our customers experienced something similar with the first version of our 3D-Printed clip, which turned out to not be sturdy enough. We designed an improved version that is much, much more resistent to punishment. We could send you a new kit, along with an experimental double-sided vinyl bottom that we would make just for you. 
 

 Would that be okay?
 

 Warmly,
 __
 Gabriel 
 Co-founder 
 Lasclay
